newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW first-half profit sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: VW first-half profit sharply higher.

text.p: Volkswagen AG's first-half profit surged 73 percent to 488 million marks ($268.6 million) despite a rise of only 12 percent in global sales, the world's fourth-largest automaker said Monday.

The German automaker -- which sells vehicles under the VW, Skoda, SEAT and Audi brands -- said company net profit rose to 488 million marks ($268.6 million) from 282 million marks ($155.2 million) in the 1996 period. Sales rose to 56.55 billion marks ($31.12 billion) from 50.5 billion marks ($27.79 billion).

At the parent level, which reflects Volkswagen sales , VW said net profit rose 20 percent to 276 million marks ($152 miillion) from 230 million marks ($127 million), while sales rose to 27.09 billion marks ($14.91 billion) from 25.86 billion marks ($14.23 billion) in the year-ago period.
VW noted it was having trouble in the German market, saying sales during the period fell to 511,088 vehicles from 515,142 vehicles in 1996's first half.
One factor for the weaker German sales cited by analysts is potential buyers waiting for the launch of the new Golf model this fall at the Frankfurt car show.
Despite weak sales at home, VW said its global vehicle sales rose 9 percent to 2.185 million units from 2.015 million units in the 1996 period.
Production in the VW unit rose to 2.207 million vehicles, up 8 percent from 2.040 million, while vehicle deliveries rose 10 percent to 2.194 million units from 1.996 million.
